explanation: The response supplies a clear, testable processing hypothesis and a matched baseline-versus-processed comparison, but it is neither a reconstruction of the reported refractory-alloy study nor a well-supported alternative. The hidden study added equimolar Ta-Nb-V over x = 0.1-0.9 to as-cast HfZrTi, producing composition-dependent HCP, omega, and BCC structures. Its central mechanism combined BCC stabilization and solid-solution strengthening with adiabatic shear localization, fragmentation, and oxidation of exposed Hf/Zr in air. The generated answer instead proposes an unvalidated heterogeneous-grain forging route and cites unrelated HEAs that establish only broad dynamic-deformation behavior. Its experiment could assess strength, hardening, and shear bands, but it lacks direct measurements of ignition time, luminous intensity, fragmentation, and oxidation energy release. A discriminating test would also require SHPB loading near 4000 s^-1 in controlled air, high-speed imaging, thresholded luminous-pixel analysis, and an inert-atmosphere control.
